precepts.text: For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen, saith the Lord of hosts. That is the offering of Judah and Jerusalem.
precepts.point: And he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver: and he shall purify the sons of Levi, and purge them as gold and silver, that they may offer unto the Lord an offering in righteousness. Then shall the offering of Judah and Jerusalem be pleasant unto the Lord, as in the days of old, and as in former years.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
Malachi 3 ends with the refined people offering again: “Then shall the offering of Judah and Jerusalem be pleasant unto the Lord, as in the days of old, and as in former years.” What is the offering of Judah and Jerusalem? Malachi already said it in the first chapter.

“For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen, saith the Lord of hosts.”

Incense offered unto his name, and a pure offering. That is the offering in righteousness that the purified sons of Levi will offer after the Lord sits as a refiner and purifier of silver: a pure offering, with his name great from the rising of the sun to the going down of it.

precepts.text: Yet I loved Jacob, just like he loved Abel, and I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste: allowed him to be overthrown. Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished: we lost all, we're going back to being vagabonds. But we will return and build the desolate places: build up ourselves as an empire, like Cain built that city. They shall build, but I will throw down. And they shall call them the border of wickedness: the beginning and the end of wickedness. And the people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever: no repentance, no salvation, no kingdom, ever. Not even the good ones, so some of you coons out there.
precepts.point: The Bible calls the evil man, or the violent man, the wicked. Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the violent man, who have purposed to overthrow my goings.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
The evil man and the violent man of Psalms 140 has a name, and Malachi gives it. “I have loved you, saith the Lord.” Israel asks, “Wherein hast thou loved us?” And the answer: “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” He loved Jacob just like he loved Abel, and he hated Esau. Laying his mountains and his heritage waste means God allowed him to be overthrown.

“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished”: we lost all, we are going back to being vagabonds. “but we will return and build the desolate places”: build themselves back up as an empire, just like Cain built that city. And the Lord answers, “They shall build, but I will throw down.”

“and they shall call them, The border of wickedness”: the beginning and the end of wickedness. “and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever”: no repentance, no salvation, no kingdom, ever. Not even the good ones, so some of you coons out there.

So when David prays “Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man” and “Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked”, this is who he is praying against: Esau, Edom, the people the Lord hated and against whom he hath indignation for ever.

precepts.text: Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom. There is no argument; Esau is Edom, and Esau came out red from his mother, hairy like a garment.
precepts.point: Was not Esau Jacob's brother? Yet I loved Jacob: Jacob and all his descendants, the twelve tribes, the whole nation of Israel. And I hated Esau: and all his nation.

note.label: I Come In Peace

precepts.why:
Malachi moves from one name to the other. God says “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau,” and then in the next breath, “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished.” He goes from Esau to Edom because they are the same man. Genesis 36:8 settles it: “Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.” There is no argument. Esau is Edom, the one who came out of his mother red, hairy like a garment, and whose name was changed to Edom, meaning red. He became the father of the Edomite nations.

So when Malachi says “I loved Jacob,” it is Jacob and all his descendants, the twelve tribes, the whole nation of Israel. When he says “I hated Esau,” it is Esau and all his nation. God does love us, even though, looking at our condition in the ghetto with everything going wrong, we ask “Wherein hast thou loved us?”

Edom said, “We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places.” Living in the Caucasus Mountains and in the caves, they came back; it is called the Renaissance. They built major cities and took control of the whole earth. But “They shall build, but I will throw down”: the Lord, the God of war, will tear it down.

“they shall call them, The border of wickedness”: not him, but them, all of them. There is not one righteous Edomite in that verse, and no one can make the Bible say what it does not say. They are “The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” Indignation is anger aroused by something unjust, unworthy, and Esau is both. Forever means forever. If the Lord has indignation against them forever, the Christian who argues they can be saved has been drugged by his religion.

precepts.text: Edom shall be called the border of wickedness and the people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.
precepts.point: What hast thou to do to take my covenant in thy mouth: one group of Esau took the new covenant as Christians and the land of America, the other took the old covenant in 1948 as Jews and the land of Israel, and both hate instruction and cast God's words behind them.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
“But unto the wicked God saith”. Who is the wicked? Malachi gives the name: “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places”. Edom is Esau, Mount Seir; it is the same subject.

But “thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” They shall call Edom the border of wickedness. And note it says the people, not the person. The apologists like to play word games and say it is talking about the person Esau. No: people is plural, meaning all of them. And how long is the Lord's indignation against them? For ever.

So the psalm is speaking to Edom: “What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” Esau said in Ezekiel 35:10, “These two nations and these two countries shall be mine”: the kingdoms of Judah and Israel, and the two countries America and Israel. They took America as Christians and the land of Israel as Jewish people.

One group of Esau took the new covenant as Christians and took the land. The other group, in 1948, took the old covenant and said, we are the Jews. Whether they call themselves Jewish or Christian, they hate instruction and cast God's words behind them. They are the wicked, the border of wickedness.

precepts.text: I hated Esau and laid his heritage waste, the Dark Ages. Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build: that is the Renaissance, when they returned and enslaved us. They shall build, but I will throw down, and men shall call them the border of wickedness, the people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.
precepts.point: When the Lord awakes and intervenes, he shall despise their image. That image is Cesare Borgia, the fake Jesus who represents all Edom.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
Job 9:24 says the wicked has the earth. Malachi names him: “And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” That is the Dark Ages, when God made Esau poverty-stricken.

“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places”. They returned in the time called the Renaissance, and that is when they conquered us and made us their slaves, Christian slaves. “thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down”. God said, I will give you a chance to build: they built up America, England, France, Germany, Australia, all those places they robbed and pillaged.

“and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” Indignation means righteous anger, for ever. So it identifies who the wicked is: Esau, Edom.

That is why Asaph saw him prospering: wherever Esau goes, it seems whatever he touches turns to gold. But he is building only to be thrown down.

precepts.text: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked.
precepts.point: I loved Jacob and hated Esau and laid his mountains waste. They shall call them the border of wickedness, the people against whom the Lord hath indignation forever.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
“The burden of the word of the Lord to Israel by Malachi.” “I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste”. That is what Paul refers to in Romans 9 when he says, as it is written. Esau went through some things at different times: they became the cavemen, came out of the caves and started taking people's identity, the fugitives and vagabonds that they were. But his ultimate, permanent judgment was deferred for a set time. “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places”, and during the Renaissance they did. “They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.”

Job shows why he has the power for now: “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, and who is he?” The border of wickedness is the mark; people will know. And the indignation for ever tells you judgment was reserved for him, but God needed to use him for a time for his plan.

If not, who is he? If it is not Esau, if it is not the United States of America, who is it? The prophets saw visions of rooms like this: the president seated up high with the vice president and the speaker beside him, and the United Nations the same on a bigger scale, all the nations with their hierarchies on one accord. That is why the scriptures say they were confederate.

It is like Cain: he was supposed to be judged, pleaded, and the Lord put a mark on him and deferred it. Revenge is a dish best served cold. How much better to let this man get so high in power and authority that he thinks he can stop God, and then take him down.

precepts.text: Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.
precepts.point: I loved Jacob and hated Esau and laid his mountains waste. They shall call them the border of wickedness, the people against whom the Lord hath indignation forever.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
Esau's judgment was deferred for a time, and Christ gave the time: “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.”

There is a set time that has to be fulfilled for these heathen nations, starting with Esau at the top: the same spirit of Cain in rulership. But it is temporary.

Through the process of time, waiting generation after generation for his judgment, Esau has forgotten it, or at least his pomp and pride make him think he is untouchable. Obadiah says, “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”, “that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” And who blames him? Look at what they just did to the air defenses Russia and China supplied. Trump now talks like that, of taking Venezuela and coming after Colombia and Mexico, and boasts that it was so fast and violent.

But it is prophesied who will bring him down. All those he dealt with will turn against him, and then Christ and his elect will have the glory and the honor to take him down. “evil shall hunt the violent man to overthrow him.” When the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled, his time is up.

precepts.text: They shall call them, The border of wickedness.
precepts.point: Testifying today means naming them which say they are Jews and are not, and calling Edom the border of wickedness.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places”. Esau is going to rebuild. But “thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down”. When the Lord comes back he is going to destroy all the cities Esau built. This is the testimony God gave Malachi, the same kind of record John bare.

“And they shall call them”: the “they” are the witnesses, the prophets. We are the ones that call them “The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.”

So the testimony is to let the Caucasian race know that God hates them forever. That is you testifying; that is the law and the testimony. The prophets wrote it, John bare record of it, and God’s witnesses on this earth today speak it.

precepts.text: Unto the wicked God saith, what hast thou to do to declare my statutes?
precepts.point: Esau is the same people from the youngest to the oldest.

note.label: Political Power Under Darkness

precepts.why:
“And I hated Esau.” God said he hates Esau, and Esau is the white man. “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places.” That is the rebirth, the Renaissance: we will build. “They shall build, but I will throw down”, which they call the dark ages, “and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.”

Keep in mind it says the people. A lot of us think they are not the same. Oh, they are the same, from the little baby all the way to the oldest. Some of them are more iced than others and show it more, but make no mistake: every single one of them hates your guts. They are all Edomites, the same people.

David shows what God says to that wicked people: “But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” Esau is the wicked. Esau has no business opening the Bible at all.

That is why it makes no sense for an Israelite to go into a debate with Esau over the Bible. We teach that the scripture says Esau is not going to get the kingdom. Why would I debate him over John 3:16 to prove to him he is going to get the kingdom? Do not be concerned with Esau. He is not even supposed to open the Bible.

precepts.text: Lucifer, cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations.
precepts.point: Esau is the same people from the youngest to the oldest.

note.label: Political Power Under Darkness

precepts.why:
The Lord hated Esau and calls his people “The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” Isaiah shows what that people does in the earth: “How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” Esau weakens the nations.

How? Economic, political and military power. Look at what Donald Trump is doing in Venezuela and in Africa right now. They bombed Nigeria on Christmas Day and claimed it was to protect Christians from persecution. They bombed Venezuela and claimed it was to stop drug trafficking, while Mexico, on America's own border, has more drug cartels than any place in the world. They want the oil. Later Trump said it plainly, return the oil to our land, as if Venezuela ever stole oil or land from America. The rich think the poor are stupid and will believe anything, and our people believe it.

And America always puts a black face on it. Before they attacked Iraq it was Colin Powell, lying about weapons of mass destruction. Before they bombed a black nation for its oil, they did not pick a lawyer, a doctor or an engineer. They picked a hoe, the same black woman who was shaking her behind, reading what they told her to read about defending Christians in Nigeria. That is the ultimate disrespect to black people.

The hypocrisy is plain. In Jerusalem the so-called Jews say they spit on the ground when they see a crucifix, call for killing Christians, and spit in a Christian woman's face in the street, and nobody bombs them to defend Christians. There is no truth in the white man. If he says look up, you better look down.

Micah shows the same people: “Woe to them that devise iniquity, and work evil upon their beds! when the morning is light, they practise it, because it is in the power of their hand. And they covet fields, and take them by violence.” The oil in Nigeria and Venezuela, the diamonds and the copper in Africa. America was built by violence on stolen land. That is Lucifer weakening the nations, and why God says, “Never trust thine enemy.”

precepts.text: Though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down.
precepts.point: They shall build, but God will throw down.

note.label: Christmas/ Icons, Idolatry, White Supremacy !!revealed!!

precepts.why:
Obadiah is spoken “concerning Edom”, the same Esau that God hated in Malachi. “Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.” God made him low, and he hated it.

“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” That is the one who dwelt in the cliffs of the rocks, in the mountains: cave dwellers, Caucasians, troglodytes. He was displaced out of his land and ended up in the Caucasus Mountains, and when he gained power on the earth he said in his heart that nobody could bring him down.

“Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle”: Greece, Rome, Spain, Portugal, they all rose up as the eagle, and America rose up as the eagle. “And though thou set thy nest among the stars”: gaining power out in space, space travel. How did he get to the stars? Because Satan gave him power to do it: technology, rockets, rocket science, nuclear bombs.

“Thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.” It is the same thing God said in Malachi. Edom said “we will return and build the desolate places”: the Renaissance, the rebirth, building up Europe into a superpower on the earth. “They shall build, but I will throw down”. They will rise up again in power, but the Most High himself will bring them down, and they are “the border of wickedness”, the beginning and the end of all wickedness on the earth, with his people, “against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.”

precepts.text: Cursed be the deceiver which hath in his flock a male, and sacrificeth unto the Lord a corrupt thing; the priests corrupted the law of the unblemished male.
precepts.point: In the book of Malachi the priests were finessing and corrupting this law: a man would bring a male without blemish, and the priest would keep it and sacrifice a blemished one, with a broken leg or a blind eye. That corruption is even more of a reason why Christ had to come and be the perfect sacrifice once and for all.

note.label: Leviticus 1: The Law of the Burnt Offerings

precepts.why:
The burnt sacrifice of the herd had to be “a male without blemish”, offered “of his own voluntary will at the door of the tabernacle.” In the book of Malachi the priests were finessing and corrupting this law: a man would bring a male without blemish, and the priest would keep it and sacrifice a blemished one, with a broken leg or a blind eye.

The Lord answers that: “But cursed be the deceiver, which hath in his flock a male, and voweth, and sacrificeth unto the Lord a corrupt thing: for I am a great King, saith the Lord of hosts, and my name is dreadful among the heathen.” The priests corrupted the law of the unblemished male, and that corruption is even more of a reason why Christ had to come and be the perfect sacrifice once and for all.

precepts.text: Edom says we are impoverished but we will return and build the desolate places, yet the Most High will throw them down and call them the border of wickedness, the people against whom he has indignation forever.
precepts.point: People say we did not do that, it is not our fault you are in poverty, the war on drugs; but if they are not the wicked the Bible speaks of, then who is and where is he, because according to his works and who he is, he is the wicked. We are talking about the Edomite nations, and it does not matter if they come from Russia, Poland, Greece, or Rome, they are the same people.

note.label: Job 9: No Man Can Contend With God

precepts.why:
“The earth is given into the hand of the wicked”. Job is pleading his case, saying he cannot speak against God, but this one thing he does see: the earth is handed to the wicked. Who are the wicked according to the Bible? It is Edom, Esau. “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.”

This is prophetic. During Job's time Esau was in the clefts of the rocks, the cave peoples, and he was not rich, but the wicked always prosper. Now they prosper with the buildings, the Maseratis, the new Hummers, while the righteous of the Most High are steady being afflicted, getting a little mercy, coming through, staying strong. They shall build, but the Most High will throw down, and they are called the border of wickedness, the people against whom he has indignation for ever.

The Most High destroyeth both the perfect and the wicked, for every man has his time under the sun; the righteous perish off the earth and the wicked perish off the earth, but we have different judgments at the end. And he covereth the faces of the judges thereof: the judges are the Israelites, the saints, for we have a book of Judges. People say only God can judge me, but that will not fly, because those who know his laws and keep his statutes and commandments are able to judge the small matters between brother and brother, sister and sister, neighbors, and situations in the church.

precepts.text: Edom, the so-called white man or red man, says they will build the desolate places, but the Most High calls them the border of wickedness, the people against whom he has indignation forever.
precepts.point: Keep me as the apple of the eye, hide me under the shadow of thy wings. This prayer asks to be kept safe from the wicked that oppress him and from his deadly enemies who compass him about.

note.label: Psalm 17: Keep Me as the Apple of the Eye

precepts.why:
David prays to be kept “From the wicked that oppress me, from my deadly enemies, who compass me about.” Malachi names that wicked oppressor: Edom, the so-called white man or red man.

“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down”. Edom says they will build the desolate places, but the Most High says he will throw it down.

And he gives them their name: “they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” Edom is the border of wickedness, the people the Most High has indignation against forever. That is the wicked David asks to be hidden from under the shadow of the Most High's wings.

precepts.text: Edom is the border of wickedness, the beginning and ending of all wickedness; a border is where something starts and where it ends, and that border of wickedness is Esau, who is the wicked one doing all this boasting.
precepts.point: The transgression of the wicked says there is no fear of God before his eyes, for he flatters himself in his own eyes. He boasts himself up: nobody could take me down.

note.label: Psalm 36: The Transgression of the Wicked

precepts.why:
Who is the wicked one doing all this boasting? “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” Edom is the border of wickedness.

A border is where something starts and where it ends. Edom is the beginning and the ending of all wickedness, and that border of wickedness is Esau. He is the one who flatters himself in his own eyes, whose mouth is iniquity and deceit, and who “deviseth mischief upon his bed”. Esau does this all the time; they devise iniquity on their beds, and the Lord has indignation against them for ever.

precepts.text: Esau is the border of wickedness, the one we are saved from.
precepts.point: The salvation of the righteous is of the Most High; he is their strength in the time of trouble and delivers them from the wicked because they trust in him. That is why salvation is so important: we get saved from the wicked.

note.label: Psalm 37: Fret Not Because of Evildoers

precepts.why:
“But the salvation of the righteous is of the Lord: he is their strength in the time of trouble. And the Lord shall help them, and deliver them: he shall deliver them from the wicked, and save them, because they trust in him.” Who is the wicked we are saved from? “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” Esau is the border of wickedness, the one we are saved from.

That is why salvation is so important: we get saved from the wicked. “I have seen the wicked in great power, and spreading himself like a green bay tree. Yet he passed away, and, lo, he was not: yea, I sought him, but he could not be found.” That is the destruction of the wicked, and the ones who see the salvation and live through it are going to make it. That is my prayer, that I make it.

precepts.text: Whereas Edom saith they will return and build the desolate places, the Most High of hosts will throw down, and they shall be called the border of wickedness and the people against whom the Most High hath indignation forever.
precepts.point: The wicked hate instruction and cast the words behind them; when they saw a thief they consented, and when Babylon came to raze Jerusalem Esau was there saying raze it, partaking with the thief against his brother Jacob.

note.label: Psalm 50: The Mighty God Judges His People and the Wicked

precepts.why:
The wicked the Most High speaks to is Esau, the so-called white man, the number one culprit on his list. “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” The Most High himself calls Edom the border of wickedness for ever.

So when he asks, “What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?”, that is Esau he is talking to. The covenant is not for the nations. The Edomite on the street preaching a new covenant for all nations is not according to the Most High.
